Embassy of Sweden in Bangladesh and the Centre for Policy Dialogue

What will make a green transition possible?

Securing Green Transition of the Textile and Readymade Garments Sector in Bangladesh

ROLE

Visiting Research Fellow (Economist) — led the research and implementation team

PERIOD / PORTFOLIO

January 2022 – June 2023

GEOGRAPHY

Bangladesh

THE ASSIGNMENT
ContextContributionRelated expertise

Research and Advocacy Program

The question
behind the work.

Research into the policy, institutional and financing barriers facing Bangladesh’s textile and ready-made garment industries.

To contribute towards enhancing environmentally sustainable and climate-neutral growth in Bangladesh with productive employment opportunities for women and youth. Developed policy and action frameworks to enable sustainable business models for green investment, and recommended reforms for strengthening institutional governance, rules and regulations in the textile industry.

PROJECT / RESEARCH SCOPE

Survey of 400 randomly selected firms, 120 key informant interviews, 8 focus group discussions

Analytical contribution.

  1. 01

    Identified critical barriers and drivers of the Green Transition within the industry, and analyzed the landscape of policies, regulations, and green financing in Bangladesh.

  2. 02

    Assessed available funds, incentives, and challenges in accessing finance for renewable energy integration.

  3. 03

    Examined the knowledge, interest, and capacity of firms in adopting green practices, and stakeholder dynamics across the Industrial Policy and global value chain.

  4. 04

    Orchestrated a research-based policy study from inception to completion — proposal, research methodology, questionnaires, and data analysis.

  5. 05

    Conducted stakeholder consultations with government agencies, banks, investors, and factory owners to identify financing gaps.

  6. 06

    Prepared policy briefs and recommendations including the introduction of a Carbon (Green) Tax and incentives for renewable energy investments.

  7. 07

    Led the survey "Barriers to Green Transition" — 400 firms, 120 KIIs, 8 FGDs.
